subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
skillName: Life Cycles of Plants and Animals
intro: Every living thing has a life cycle, the stages it goes through during its life. Life cycles are diverse and can look very different: a butterfly changes from egg to caterpillar to chrysalis to adult, a frog goes from egg to tadpole to adult, and a plant grows from a seed into a plant that makes new seeds. Even though the details differ, all life cycles share the same key stages: being born or sprouting (birth), getting bigger (growth), making new living things (reproduction), and eventually dying (death). A model, like a cycle diagram with arrows, can show these stages.

items.prompt: A butterfly goes from egg to caterpillar to chrysalis to adult. What stages of a life cycle does this show, and which stages do all organisms share?

steps: The butterfly starts as an egg (birth), grows as a caterpillar (growth), and becomes an adult that lays eggs (reproduction).
All organisms share these same stages: birth, growth, reproduction, and death, even though the details differ.
solution.answer: It shows birth, growth, reproduction, and death, which all organisms share even though their cycles look different.

items.prompt: Compare the life cycle of a frog and a plant. How are they different, and what do they have in common?

steps: A frog goes egg to tadpole to adult, while a plant goes seed to sprout to mature plant.
The stages look very different between them.
But both share birth, growth, reproduction, and death, the common parts of every life cycle.
solution.answer: The stages look different, but both share birth, growth, reproduction, and death.

items.prompt: Why do we say all organisms have life cycles even though they look so different?

steps: Each kind of organism has its own stages that may look unique.
Still, every organism is born or sprouts, grows, can reproduce, and dies.
Because all share these four stages, they all have life cycles even if the details differ.
solution.answer: Because every organism is born, grows, reproduces, and dies, even though the stages look different.

items.prompt: Name the four stages that all life cycles have in common.

steps: Every life cycle shares the same key stages.
They are birth, growth, reproduction, and death.

items.prompt: A student draws a model of a plant's life cycle. What should the arrows show, and why is it drawn as a cycle?

steps: The arrows show the plant going from seed to sprout to grown plant that makes new seeds.
The new seeds start the cycle over again.
It is drawn as a cycle because reproduction makes new organisms that begin the stages again.
solution.answer: The arrows show seed to plant to new seeds, drawn as a cycle because reproduction starts the stages over.

items.prompt: A pet dog is born, grows up, has puppies, and later grows old and dies. Match each event to a life cycle stage.

steps: Being born is the birth stage, and growing up is the growth stage.
Having puppies is reproduction, and growing old and dying is the death stage.
So the dog's life shows all four common stages of a life cycle.
solution.answer: Born = birth, growing up = growth, having puppies = reproduction, dying = death.
